chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
Al-Mubarat (mutual separation) is a final divorce, and there is no revocation (raj'ah) in it.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Right of revocation (taking back the wife without new contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling of Mubarat in Shia Islam regarding revocability?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that 'al-Mubarat' is a distinct form of divorce where both parties mutually agree to separate, typically involving the wife compensating the husband, and it carries the ruling of a final, irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in). Unlike the revocable divorce, the husband cannot reclaim the wife during the waiting period (iddah) without a new marriage contract, emphasizing the finality of this mutual agreement. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between unilateral and consensual divorce mechanisms.
